items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the private housing finance law and the state finance law, in
relation to enacting the "housing our neighbors with dignity act"
items.lawCode: Add Art 31 §§1280 - 1282, Priv Hous Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5257

SPONSOR: GIANARIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the private housing finance law and the state finance
law, in relation to enacting the "housing our neighbors with dignity
act"

 
PURPOSE:

To provide affordable permanent housing that meets standards established
to ensure safety, habitability, quality, and access to supportive
services as appropriate, for low-income households and people experienc-
ing homeless through the state's purchase and conversion of distressed
hotels and commercial properties in cities with a population of one
million or more.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one titles the act.

Section two amends the private housing finance law by adding a new arti-
cle 31 which details the legislative findings and purposes, definitions,
and Housing our Neighbors with Dignity Program. The program will provide
a mechanism for the state to purchase, acquire, restore, and hold
distressed commercial real estate for the purposes of maintaining or
increasing affordable housing in New York City for two years following
the effective date of the act. These properties will then be sold or
otherwise transferred to entities that will use such property to guaran-
tee affordable, habitable, and environmentally sustainable housing to
asset-limited, low-income individuals and families. At least 50% of the
converted properties will be set aside for those experiencing homeless.
Affordable housing at these properties will be limited to those house-
holds with income at or below 50% of the area median income for the
county in which the property is located. Tenants of the affordable hous-
ing units will have full tenancy rights, and will have rent obligations
set at no more than 30% of their income.

Section three amends the state finance law by adding a new section 99-ii
which establishes a distressed property conversion fund which will be
used to finance the Housing our Neighbors with Dignity Program.

Section four sets the effective date.

 
EXISTING LAW:

 
JUSTIFICATION:

New York State faces an ongoing financial and public health crisis
related to housing. Currently, the number of homeless single adults in
New York City is 132% higher than it was ten years ago and has hit a
record 20,000 people in shelters as of October 2020. Additionally, New
York City has an unmet need for sub-50% AMI housing. Even prior to the
pandemic, as many as 580,000 New Yorkers are either rent burdened, over-
crowded, or living in long-term shelters according to the City Comp-
troller.


At the same time, the pandemic has hit New York's hotel industry hard;
in fact, as many as 25,000 rooms, or 20% of New York's total, may not
reopen. As a result, more than 25,000 hotel employees have been out of
work for more than six months. Moreover, according to CBRE Hotels
Research, US lodging demand is "forecast to increase by a compound annu-
al growth rate of 14.1% over the next four years, recovering to 2019
levels by Q3 2023."

This bill puts New York on a pathway to social housing with permanent
affordability. The state would also not be alone in implementing this
kind of solution. California has already taken steps to establish a
policy, known as the "HomeKey" program, to convert distressed hotels to
permanent housing utilizing federal funds.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

TBD

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

TBD

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become a law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or
repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation of
this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and completed
on or before such effective date.

BILL NUMBER: S5257A

SPONSOR: GIANARIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the private housing finance law, the state finance law
and the multiple dwelling law, in relation to enacting the "housing our
neighbors with dignity act"

 
PURPOSE:

To provide affordable permanent housing that meets standards established
to ensure safety, habitability, quality, and access to supportive
services as appropriate, for low- and moderate-income households and
people experiencing homeless through the state's purchase or financing
of purchase, holding, and conversion of distressed hotels and commercial
office properties.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one titles the act.

Section two amends the private housing finance law by adding a new arti-
cle 31 which details the legislative findings and purposes, definitions,
and Housing our Neighbors with Dignity Program. The program will provide
a mechanism for the state to purchase or finance the purchase, acquire,
restore, and hold distressed hotels and commercial office real estate
for the purposes of maintaining or increasing permanently affordable
housing in New York State. These properties will then be owned, oper-
ated, and managed by appropriate nonprofit organizations. Appropriate
nonprofit organizations will be designated via a vetting process devel-
oped by DHCR. At least 50% of the converted properties will be set aside
for those experiencing homeless. Requirements for what each unit must
contain is also outlined. Affordable housing will be achieved by ensur-
ing that the new housing achieves income averaging at or below 50% of
AMI, with residents' eligibility capped at a maximum of 80% AMI at the
start of their lease. In the case of a hotel property at which the prop-
erty owner of such property is a signatory to a collective bargaining
agreement, the property owner must certify prior to the state initiating
the purchase, acquisition, or holding that the collective bargaining
representative has mutually agreed with the property owner to take such
action. Tenants of the affordable housing units will have full tenancy
rights, will have rent stabilization in localities that have adopted or
opted into the rent stabilization law, and will have rent obligations
set at no more than 30% of their income.

Section three amends section 301 of the multiple dwelling law to add a
new subdivision 7 which provides that any certificate by the department
authorizing occupancy of a dwelling as a Class B hotel shall also
authorize occupancy of units in such dwelling for permanent residence
purposes notwithstanding any provision of this chapter or of any state
law, local law, ordinance, resolution or regulation that would otherwise
prohibit such occupancy, require a change or alteration to the dwelling,
or require a new or amended certificate provided that such occupancy for
permanent residence purposes shall be subject to the approval of the
local housing agency in its discretion; a portion of such dwelling shall
be located within four hundred feet of a district that under the local
zoning regulations or ordinances permits residential uses and such
dwelling shall not be located in an industrial business zone established
pursuant to chapter six-D of title twenty-two of the administrative code
of the city of New York; and such dwelling shall meet the conditions in
paragraph b of this subdivision. It also outlines circumstances under
which occupancy of units in a dwelling shall not be authorized under the
provisions of paragraph a of the subdivi sion unless such units are
purchased, acquired, or financed.

Section four amends the state finance law by adding a new section 99-ii
which establishes a social housing conversion fund which will be used to
finance the Housing our Neighbors with Dignity Program.

Section five sets the effective date.

record 20,000 people in shelters as of October 2020. Additionally, even

work for more than six months. Moreover, according to CBRE Hotels

al growth rate of 14.1% over the next four years, recovering to 2019
levels by Q3 2023."

affordability. The state would also not be alone in implementing this
kind of solution. California has already taken steps to establish a
policy, known as the "HomeKey" program, to convert distressed hotels to
permanent housing utilizing federal funds.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 17 Chapter 396
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 5257-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the private housing finance law, in relation to
        enacting the housing our neighbors with dignity act"
 
    APPROVED
 
  The bill will create the Housing Our Neighbors with  Dignity  Program,
which  will  help  provide affordable housing to homeless and low-income
New Yorkers. The legislation allows the Housing Trust  Fund  Corporation
to  finance  the purchase, acquisition, holding, or conversion of hotels
and commercial office properties to  be  used  as  permanent  affordable
housing owned by not-for-profit organizations, with access to supportive
housing  as  appropriate.  The  bill  will  further grant tenants of the
affordable housing units full tenancy rights, and, will subject units to
rent stabilization in localities that have adopted or  opted  into  rent
stabilization.  Finally,  the  bill will require notification to and the
assent of any applicable hotel worker  collective  bargaining  organiza-
tion's  representative  for  the  acquisition  of  the  property for the
Program.
 
  I am supportive of this bill and believe that it will help to  address
some  of  the  problems  posed  by  the housing crisis in New York City.
However, several changes are necessary to help maximize  the  impact  of
the  program. Technical fixes are necessary, such as revising the target
that 50% of properties be set aside for homeless New Yorkers to  50%  of
units be set aside for the homeless. Clarifying changes are necessary to
ensure  that  the  funds  under  the  Housing Our Neighbors with Dignity
Program may be used for the conversion of hotel or office space for  the
purposes of this program, and not only for the acquisition of such prop-
erty.    Additionally,  we have agreed to eliminate the requirement that
the Housing Trust Fund Corporation help find appropriate  properties  to
finance, which would be unduly burdensome on the Corporation, and clari-
fied  that provisions of this program are subject to the availability of
appropriated funds.
 
  Finally, we have agreed  to  increase  the  Area  Median  income  from
50%-60%,  and  modify the required refrigerator size from 24 inches to a
capacity of 7 cubic feet, to provide greater flexibility in the develop-
ment of properties under this legislation.
 
  With these changes, I am pleased to sign this bill into law.
 
  The bill is approved.                       (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______

summary: Enacts the "Housing Our Neighbors with Dignity act" in order to provide a mechanism for the state to finance the acquisition of distressed hotels and commercial office properties by the appropriate nonprofit organizations for the purpose of maintaining or increasing affordable housing.
title: Enacts the "Housing Our Neighbors with Dignity act"
